summary: High-frequency API key rotations and transient user-impersonation events after external campaign click
description:
Issue summary: Several internal service and user accounts began performing rapid API key rotations and short-lived impersonation calls shortly after a subset of employees clicked an external marketing/survey link. Impact: Potential privilege escalation and unauthorized repository reads; elevated risk to CI credentials and automated deploy hooks. Initial detection triggered by anomaly detection alerts on the secrets-rotation monitoring dashboard.

Observed scope: ~8 distinct identities (mix of human and service principals) with ~50 rotation events in a 90-minute window. At least 3 deploy pipelines retried due to token refresh failures. No confirmed exfiltration of customer data at the time of writing.

Environment details: Production tenant: redwood-main. Region: us-east-1. Affected SSO IdP: corp-okta. Tokens observed were short-lived (TTL ~5–10m) and originated from a small set of external IPs (geo: EU/Baltic).
timeline: 2026-03-12 09:12 UTC — Employee A reports suspicious marketing email with an embedded survey link to #security-ops
2026-03-12 09:18 UTC — IDS flagged high-frequency key rotation pattern for service-principal 'ci/deploy-batcher'
2026-03-12 09:31 UTC — WAF logged outbound redirect to third-party shortlink domain; security-ops begins triage
2026-03-12 10:05 UTC — Additional accounts observed: two dev users and five service principals with similar rotation behavior
2026-03-12 10:50 UTC — Automated rollback of affected CI pipelines initiated to prevent deployment flaps
2026-03-12 11:30 UTC — Initial containment: revoked recently issued API keys and disabled affected service principals' sessions
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Clicked a marketing/survey shortlink sent to multiple employees
2) Shortlink redirects to a page that issued a cross-origin form POST to a third-party tracking domain
3) The tracking domain triggered an OAuth device/consent flow redirect that attempted silent token exchange against our IdP
4) Silent exchange appeared to succeed for ephemeral tokens which then triggered backend rotation workflows for linked service principals

comments: Anika Shah (Reporter) 2026-03-12T09:26: Assigned to on-call SRE and security-ops — initial containment recommended: rotate affected keys, block outbound to trk-short.ly, and capture full PCAPs for any host that clicked the link.
Liam O'Connor (Assignee) 2026-03-12T09:40: Confirmed initial revocations for keys issued after 09:00 UTC. I'm collecting token exchange logs from corp-okta; tagging IAM team.

Priya Menon (IAM) 2026-03-12T10:12: Observed unusual 'prompt=none' token_exchange calls from third-party redirectors. We're temporarily enforcing stricter 'prompt' policy and invalidating recent silent-exchange sessions.
SRE Team 2026-03-12T11:02: We've rate-limited rotation APIs and applied a temporary rule to refuse key rotations triggered by webhook origins outside allowlist. Monitoring for pipeline failures.
Security Ops 2026-03-12T12:00: Outreach to employees who clicked the link (A, B, C) for host scans; recommending passwordless session revocation and device re-check.

Liam O'Connor 2026-03-14T08:30: Early forensics: IPs map to a known tracking vendor previously used in targeted campaign; correlating with marketing provider's send list. Follow-up with Legal and Marketing required.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Third-party marketing link included a chained redirect to a tracking domain that attempted silent OAuth exchanges; surrogate cookies or CORS misconfig enabled token-less refreshes for some sessions.

Hypothesis 2: A compromised marketing vendor account allowed insertion of a small JS snippet that calls our auth endpoints via a browser-side redirect, triggering backend rotation hooks tied to user preferences (edge-case bug).

Evidence: Token exchange logs show 'prompt=none' and 'x-forwarded-for' with two external IPs. No user password attempts recorded. The rotations were performed by our internal rotation service when it received the webhook with an apparently valid subject claim.
Partial finding: Rotation service accepts certain webhook signatures from marketing provider; signatures validated only by header token which may have been exposed via a vendor-side leak.
resolution: Containment actions executed: revoked all API keys issued after 2026-03-12 09:00 UTC for affected principals, applied temporary rotation API rate-limits, blocked known tracking domain at WAF and proxy, and enforced stricter 'prompt' semantics on silent token exchanges via IdP policy. We have not yet observed confirmed data exfiltration. Legal and Marketing notified; marketing sends paused with vendor suspended pending vendor investigation.
next_steps: 1) Full vendor audit with Marketing and Legal — completed dependency mapping and confirm if vendor credentials were leaked
2) Patch rotation-service to require signed webhook payloads with nonce validation (PR opened: github.com/redwood/rotation-service/pull/498), ETA 2026-03-20
3) Backfill alerting for 'rotation spikes' correlated with external-origin webhooks; update runbook for similar phishing-linked rotation patterns
4) Rotate long-lived CI tokens that may have been indirectly exposed as precaution — schedule during maintenance window
5) Post-incident review and postmortem to be drafted and linked here once complete
